body:
Changing initialization order is dangerous and tricky, however, this is just changing "registration order" (aka when it becomes available to GDExtension and scripting) which shouldn't affect anything internal to the the engine.

That said, it could still have interesting side-effects, like: Would using this very early allow catching `ClassDB` in an unpredictable/inconsistent state? Are there any methods on `ClassDB` that are unsafe to use very early?

Assuming we can confirm that there aren't any issues like that, I think philosophically, `ClassDB` is similar to the other low-level singletons that we have exposed very early. So, it could make sense!

For native classes from Godot, though, the language binding should have access to a lot of the information in `ClassDB` just from the `extension_api.json`. This wouldn't necessarily be up-to-date for the version of Godot that's actually running (if it was built using an `extension_api.json` from an earlier version), or for any classes added by other GDExtensions.

Can you give more details on the use-case you have for using `ClassDB` earlier?

> Can you give more details on the use-case you have for using `ClassDB` earlier?

Gladly! The registration APIs in GDExtension (such as `classdb_register_extension_class*`) are fallible, but they don't provide any status. And even if they did, it would be hard to design an error model that covers all the things that can go wrong. Yes, there is a human-readable output on the command line, but there's no programmatic interface to relay this to the user.

So instead, I'd like to perform certain validations ahead of the actual registrations, such as:
- Does the base class exist
- Is the base class "final" (i.e. non-inheritable)
- Does a name of a function/property/signal conflict with one in the base
- Extension-specific constraints (allowing a binding to be more strict than Godot itself)

Of course, some of this can be done based on the `extension_api.json`, however:
- It needs duplicating and book-keeping of a lot of state that's readily available in `ClassDB`
- It will miss anything that's not statically declared (i.e. symbols in newer Godot versions, other extensions, etc.)

It would be nice to have a version of `classdb_register_extension_class*` that produces the status results.

The first three items on the list you shared are really about assisting the developer during their development cycle to avoid making mistakes, so an error has the advantage that we can communicate with the user the problem when it happens, as opposed to having to do a lot of runtime work to call into ClassDB repeatedly to extract this information for each issue.

Many of these reflection-based solutions are great initially, and next thing you know, you have a couple hundred of these types and your startup has tanked and you are in a difficult position to fix it.   The last time I faced something like this I joked that you get your first corporate bonus getting the feature in place, and then two years later, you get two years worth of bonuses architecting the solution that does not work upfront.

Another benefit of introducing a status-reporting version of `classdb_register_extension_class` is that new invariants and issues can be reported without updating a language binding or upgrading a codebase.

> It would be nice to have a version of `classdb_register_extension_class*` that produces the status results.

I agree, but this only solves part of the issue.

First, it will be hard to make a C API expressive enough to cover all possible error cases, _and_ provide enough context for a user. Typically such a status would be a C enum, but that has many shortcomings:
- Only first error can be reported (instead of collecting everything that's wrong).
- No context information can be associated with the enum. This would need an extra struct/union.

So you'd need to come up with an elaborate nested data model that's also flexible enough to accomodate future error types, while still remaining backwards-compatible. At the same time, many callers only care about success/failure, or a human-readable stderr message.

---

Second, a status code can only be obtained _after the fact_, once registration already succeeded or failed. If a developer has a group of classes (e.g. plugin) that should be registered in an all-or-nothing fashion, how can this be done reliably? This would need complex rollback logic, which can also fail on its own or leave side effects in the engine.

If we had a way to check whether the conditions are right for all classes _before_ starting with the first, we could avoid changing engine state _at all_.

---

Last, a status code would only communicate what's allowed from Godot's own perspective. It does not allow a language binding to perform additional validations. As an example, for the Rust binding it's helpful to know if methods in a class operate on raw pointers.

`ClassDB` would provide such information. This is already possible today in _Scene_ level, but currently there's a discrepancy with the `ClassDB` singleton being missing from lower levels.

On those three cases, aren't all of these manifested as error logs?

These are not necessarily helping the static typing system, it is at best producing a different set of diagnostics for the consumer - but they would ultimately rely on the Godot output to diagnose this at this point, not a compile time error.   

Diagnostics-wise, it might also be useful to extend the error information that is logged, but this remains a risky change for producing alternative information that the engine should already provide.
